raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`_prefill_schedule_prep_kernel`, added in #37764 for the ROCm DeepSeek-V4 FP4 indexer, keeps JIT-compiling new variants while serving. Its scalars and buffer-view pointers change with every prefill batch, and Triton specializes on them. Each compile stalls the engine for ~1.5 s, and the log reports `took 1.5 s to compile after serving started`. A 20-min AgentX run logs 289 of these. AITER's `_prefill_row_plan_kernel` has the same problem (120 compiles in the same run) and is fixed in ROCm/aiter#5925.

## Modifications

- Don't specialize any of the kernel's runtime args. Only `BLOCK_T` (9 row-count buckets) is left to select a variant.
- Compile those 9 variants at backend init (~6 s). If the installed AITER provides `warmup_prefill_row_plan` (ROCm/aiter#5925), warm its row-plan kernel too.
- Warm up for the DeepSeek-V4.1 low-ratio indexers as well, which build the same schedule (they recompiled 34-46 times per prefill server in V4.1-Flash PD AgentX runs); draft workers skip it.

## Accuracy Tests

gsm8k, full test set (1319 questions), 8-shot, TP8 + DSpark:

| | main | this PR | this PR + ROCm/aiter#5925 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Accuracy | 0.945 | 0.947 | 0.955 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

AgentX on MI355X, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP8 + DSpark, conc 32, 1200 s. All three arms ran on the same node.

| | main | this PR | this PR + ROCm/aiter#5925 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_prefill_schedule_prep_kernel` serving-time compiles (8 ranks) | 289 | **0** | **0** |
| `_prefill_row_plan_kernel` serving-time compiles (8 ranks) | 120 | 97 | **0** |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 896.0 | 918.1 (+2.5%) | 934.1 (**+4.3%**) |
| TTFT avg (ms) | 3090 | 3133 (+1.4%) | 2910 (−5.8%) |
| TTFT p50 (ms) | 1445 | 1273 (−11.9%) | 1313 (−9.1%) |
| TTFT p90 (ms) | 5214 | 5507 (+5.6%) | 4577 (−12.2%) |
| ITL avg (ms) | 12.13 | 11.38 (−6.2%) | 11.35 (−6.4%) |
| ITL p50 (ms) | 11.83 | 10.93 (−7.6%) | 11.08 (−6.3%) |
| ITL p90 (ms) | 17.09 | 16.46 (−3.7%) | 15.99 (−6.4%) |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

files.patch:
@@ -20,6 +20,7 @@
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
+import functools
 from typing import Optional, Tuple
 
 import torch
@@ -62,7 +63,9 @@ def _pad_page_table_tile(
     tl.store(dst_ptr + row * dst_stride + cols, vals, mask=inside)
 
 
-@triton.jit
+# Every runtime arg varies per prefill batch (row count, table widths and strides,
+# view offsets); specializing them made the kernel recompile (~1.5 s) mid-serving.
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=range(17))
 def _prefill_schedule_prep_kernel(
     le_ptr,  # [T] int32  local_ends (== c4_seq_lens)
     chunks_ptr,  # [T] int32  out
@@ -147,6 +150,27 @@ def _prefill_schedule_prep_kernel(
         )
 
 
+@functools.cache
+def warmup_prefill_schedule_prep(device: torch.device, block_k: int = 256) -> None:
+    """Compile the prep kernel's BLOCK_T variants (its only ones) before serving."""
+    buf = torch.empty(16, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    pt = buf.view(1, 16)
+    block_t = 16
+    while block_t <= MAX_FUSED_ROWS:
+        _prefill_schedule_prep_kernel.warmup(
+            *[buf] * 7, pt, pt, *[16] * 8,
+            BLOCK_K=block_k, BLOCK_T=block_t, PT_BLOCK=_PT_BLOCK, grid=(1,),
+        )  # fmt: skip
+        block_t *= 2
+    try:  # the same fix for AITER's row plan, which newer AITER ships
+        from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels.mqa_logits.pa_mqa_logits_fp4_prefill import (
+            warmup_prefill_row_plan,
+        )
+    except ImportError:
+        return
+    warmup_prefill_row_plan(device, block_k)
+
+
 @triton.jit
 def _pad_page_table_kernel(
     src_ptr,

@@ -1034,6 +1034,14 @@ def __init__(
             )
 
             self._fp4_graph_row_limit = MAX_FUSED_ROWS
+        if not self.is_draft_worker and (
+            self.enable_deepseek_v4_fp4_indexer or self.low_ratios
+        ):
+            from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.fp4_indexer_schedule_hip import (
+                warmup_prefill_schedule_prep,
+            )
+
+            warmup_prefill_schedule_prep(self.device)
         # DSv4 C4 decode / target-verify indexer on AITER's row-group kernel: no schedule,
         # its workspace built in the graph, a request's verify rows sharing each key load.
         # Every launch reads a table of one width (its compiled variant) for the server's life.
